title: Nobody mints a long-lived credential, and nobody rewrites the deployment identities
why: The estate deploys through OIDC (GE-011): short-lived, repository-scoped, branch-scoped role assumption. An IAM user or access key created afterwards is a permanent key outside that design that nobody will rotate. Separately, the deployment roles are the boundary — a principal that can edit tenure-gha-* has every permission those roles will ever be given.
sourced_from: infrastructure/oidc/roles.tf — the three deployment roles, all named tenure-gha-*
limits: iam:CreateRole is NOT denied. The engine's deploy role creates and passes its own task roles under a name prefix (infrastructure/oidc/roles.tf), and denying role creation outright would stop the estate deploying while stopping nobody from escalating — an escalation goes through a policy, not through a role that has none.

This does not stop a principal that already holds iam:PutRolePolicy on an UNPREFIXED role from widening it. That is bounded in the role policies themselves, which confine IAM writes to a name prefix; the two controls are deliberately different mechanisms.
